institution: Technische Universität Ilmenau — Institut für Medientechnik, Fakultät Elektrotechnik und Informationstechnik
programme: M.Sc. Medieningenieurwissenschaften (formerly/also listed as Medientechnologie / Media Technology)
existsFor2027: YES. The programme page is live and TU Ilmenau's uni-assist notice states applications for all semesters starting in 2027 or later go through uni-assist. Not suspended, not biennial. NOTE: the Institute of Media Technology runs two closely related masters — the German/English 'Medieningenieurwissenschaften' and the internationally-marketed 'M.Sc. Research in Media Engineering'. The English-completable route is the latter; treat them as one family but apply to the right one.
awards: Master of Science (M.Sc.), a full German university master's degree from a state university. Programme page lists it under 'Masterstudiengänge' with the M.Sc. award. This is a genuine research master's, qualifying for doctoral study.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: YES — explicit. DAAD/TU Ilmenau entry text for the Media Engineering master: 'Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, media technology, computer engineering or computer science respectively (media) informatics with a programme duration of at least six semesters (180 credit points).' Computer science is named. The programme page's own short form is 'Abschluss eines verwandten Bachelorstudiums' (a related bachelor's). Caveat quoted alongside: 'Strong foundations in mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, and signal processing are highly recommended.' A pure software-engineering BSc has the maths and computing but usually not the signal processing.
gate: WRITTEN QUALIFYING EXAM — no portfolio, no audition, no ear test. The recorded gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' is wrong on the portfolio and on the interview. The real procedure: a points-scored subject-specific suitability review of the transcript, then, per the official qualifying-exam page: applicants scoring 50–69 points must sit the exam; 70+ are exempt; under 50 are rejected. The exam is 'a written online test' of 90 minutes, questions in English, taken via Moodle under Webex proctoring, comprising 'mathematical basics' (7 questions), 'basic knowledge from media technology areas' (28 questions) and 'scientific work' (5 questions). Pass = 'at least half of the questions from each of the three blocks...correctly (= 20 points)'. It 'cannot be waived entirely'. Offered four times yearly: late April, late July, late October, late January.
gateType: Written multiple-choice qualifying exam (academic, technical). NOT a portfolio. NOT an audition. NOT an ear test.
portfolioSpec: NONE REQUIRED. No portfolio, showreel or work sample appears anywhere in the admission procedure. This is the single most candidate-favourable fact in the whole batch — he has no portfolio and does not need one here.
costForTunisian: NO TUITION FEE. Thuringia charges no tuition for any nationality, and the décret-type differentiated-fee regime is French, not German — it does not apply. Semester contribution: 'Approx. 320 EUR per semester (including a rail/bus ticket and reduced prices in the university canteen and cafeterias)' = approx. €640/yr. Plus a one-off uni-assist handling fee of €75 for an application with non-European certificates. TOTAL ≈ €640/yr. The recorded band 'Free' is very slightly optimistic — it is free of tuition but not of the semester contribution.
funding: DAAD scholarships are the realistic route (DAAD EPOS / Study Scholarships for graduates). These are a SEPARATE, EARLIER application, not automatic on admission, and DAAD deadlines for a following-year intake typically fall around the preceding autumn. Exact 2027 DAAD amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED — not on the TU Ilmenau pages read. Deutschlandstipendium (€300/month) exists at many German universities but its availability at TU Ilmenau for this programme is UNVERIFIED.
deadline: Non-EU/EEA applicants apply through uni-assist. TU Ilmenau states applications for semesters starting 2027 or later must go via uni-assist. The customary German winter-semester deadline is 15 July for the October start, and TU Ilmenau publishes its 'Bewerbungszeiträume' separately. EXACT 2027 DATES UNVERIFIED — the deadline page did not render dates. CRITICAL SCHEDULING POINT: the qualifying exam runs only four times a year (late April / late July / late October / late January), so he must apply early enough to sit one inside his application period; missing it outside the period means 'automatic rejection'. No Campus France gate applies — Germany, not France.
language: Mixed. The programme page states 'Deutsch/Englisch'. DAAD for the sibling Media Engineering master: 'Courses are held in English (50%) and German (50%)', with the note that 'The programme can also be completed entirely in either language.' Certificate demanded: 'C1 required, please provide an official language certificate', with IELTS Academic 7 among the accepted scores (TU Ilmenau's general master minimum is B2 to apply, C1 to enrol without a preparatory course).
verdictWhy: This is the best structural fit in the batch and the only one that is genuinely near-free with no portfolio and no audition — a written technical exam is exactly the gate a software engineer can prepare for. Two things must be resolved first: an IELTS 7 / C1 English certificate, which is a serious step up from 'working English' and he has not sat the test at all; and the fact that half the teaching is nominally in German, so he must confirm in writing with the institute that his chosen master can be completed 100% in English. Also understand what this degree is: media/audio engineering and signal processing, not record production — it will not teach him to make records, it will teach him the technology under them.
correction: CONTRADICTS THE RECORDED GATE. Recorded as 'Portfolio + exam/interview'. There is no portfolio and no interview. The gate is a 90-minute proctored written multiple-choice qualifying exam, triggered only if the transcript review scores 50–69 points. ALSO CORRECTS THE RECORDED COST BAND 'Free': no tuition, but a semester contribution of approx. €320/semester (~€640/yr) plus a €75 uni-assist fee is payable.

institution: FH JOANNEUM Gesellschaft mbH — Institute of Design & Communication (in collaboration with KUG, University of …
programme: MA Interaction, Media and Sound Design — study track SOUND DESIGN
existsFor2027: YES. Live, recruiting, with a published five-round calendar for the 28.09.2026 start; the same rolling structure recurs annually. Not suspended, not biennial. The 2027 calendar is not yet published (the visible one is PRIOR CYCLE) but the pattern is stable.
awards: Master of Arts (MA) from an Austrian Fachhochschule — a full, accredited Austrian master's degree. Not a certificate or diploma course.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE, and the fine print is the problem. Headline: 'If you want to apply for this Master's degree programme you need to have a relevant Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification.' Broad list quoted: the programme accepts graduates from 'technical, artistic, humanities, social sciences, economics, natural sciences and interdisciplinary programmes' — a technical/software degree is squarely inside that list. BUT the page then requires that 80 ECTS of the prior degree align with core subject areas comparable to FH JOANNEUM's Information Design bachelor's, AND that the candidate meet at least one of: 'Relevant professional experience spanning a period of at least two years'; 'Assessment of professional aptitude based on the submitted portfolio'; 'Relevant further training or study modules with a workload equivalent of at least 30 ECTS'. He has no professional experience and no further training — so the ONLY door open to him is the portfolio route, and he has no portfolio.
gate: Online portfolio + online interview. Per the admissions-procedure page the process is 'a complete application, an assessment of the online portfolio by the admissions committee, an online interview'. The interview 'lasts approximately 20 minutes' and evaluates 'your knowledge in the field of sound design and your motivation, suitability and talent for the chosen course'. Integrity conditions quoted: applicants must 'confirm that no unauthorised aids are used and no one else is present to help' and 'present official photo identification'. NO ear-training test, NO musical audition, NO live performance, NO practical production test found anywhere in the published procedure.
gateType: Portfolio + 20-minute online interview. No audition, no ear test.
portfolioSpec: NOT PUBLISHED IN DETAIL — the admissions-requirements and admissions-procedure pages both refer to 'the online portfolio' without stating a number of pieces, durations or file formats. The Non-EU handout only says generically: 'Please note that some Bachelor and Master degree programmes require specific papers (portfolio, letters of reference, etc.) as part of the application.' The exact specification must be obtained from the online application system or from Studienberatung. UNVERIFIED at the specification level.
costForTunisian: €727 PER SEMESTER = €1,454/yr, stated verbatim in the official Non-EU/EEA handout for 2026/27: 'Cost Contribution (once a semester) + € 727 (€ 1454)'. On acceptance a third-country applicant must transfer the first two semesters (€1,454) IN ADVANCE. Separately, every third-country applicant 'must pay a deposit of €250.00 plus €10.00 reimbursement of expenses via the FH Shop before applying' — €260 payable simply to apply. Add the ÖH student-union fee (~€25/semester, ~€50/yr). Austria's new €363.36/semester Studienbeitrag introduced from autumn 2026 applies to EU/EEA starters; reporting states the third-country regime 'remains unchanged', i.e. the €727 stands instead — but whether the two stack is UNVERIFIED and worth a written question. Realistic year-one outlay ≈ €1,760; ongoing ≈ €1,505/yr.
funding: NONE IDENTIFIED on the programme or non-EU pages. No scholarship, waiver or stipend for third-country students was found. OeAD Austrian government scholarships exist nationally but eligibility for a Tunisian FH master's applicant and the 2027 deadlines are UNVERIFIED. Assume he pays in full.
deadline: Rolling, five rounds — by far the most forgiving calendar in the batch. PRIOR CYCLE (for the 28.09.2026 start), verbatim: deadline 01.02.2026 / interviews 23.02–27.02.2026; deadline 24.03.2026 / interviews 20.04–24.04.2026; deadline 27.04.2026 / interviews 11.05–15.05.2026; deadline 26.05.2026 / interviews 29.06–03.07.2026; deadline 29.06.2026 / interview 16.07.2026. The school states 'The chances of being accepted are the same for all appointments.' For a Tunisian applicant the handout warns: 'We highly recommend applying as soon as possible due to long visa procedures.' Expect the equivalent February–June 2027 windows for a September 2027 start. Exact 2027 dates UNVERIFIED. No Campus France gate — Austria, not France.
language: English. 'the programme is taught in English.' Certificate demanded, verbatim: English 'equivalent to minimum Level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages and may be provided in the form of TOEFL Certificate (min. 87 points), a TELC Certificate, a Cambridge Certificate (First Certificate in English - FCE), PTE Academic Zertifikat (Pearson Test of English; min. 59 Punkte) or an IELTS Certificate or another equivalent school certificate.' B2 only — a much lower bar than TU Ilmenau's C1. The letter of motivation and CV must be in English.
verdictWhy: Genuinely the most winnable calendar anywhere in this dataset — five shots a year, English at B2 only, no audition and no ear test, and a 20-minute interview rather than a concours. But it is gated on a portfolio he does not have, and for him the portfolio is not optional decoration: with no professional experience and no further training, the portfolio is the sole route by which he can satisfy the additional eligibility criterion at all. Build the portfolio first, then this becomes a real target. Note it is sound design for interaction and media, not record production.
correction: CONTRADICTS THE RECORDED COST BAND. Recorded 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr'. Actual tuition is €1,454/yr, which alone is just under, but the ÖH fee pushes the running cost to roughly €1,505/yr and year one carries a further €260 non-refundable application deposit plus a mandatory €1,454 advance transfer on acceptance. Treat this as 'about €1,500/yr with a €1,700+ first year', not comfortably under €1,500. The recorded gate and language are correct.

programme: Master Son (section Son) - Diplome de l'ENS Louis-Lumiere
existsFor2027: YES. The concours ran for 2026 with registration 1 December 2025 – 14 January 2026 and the school continues to admit 16 students per master. Not suspended, not biennial — annual.
awards: NOT a diplôme national de master. Verbatim from the programme page: 'Diplôme de niveau Bac+5 qui confère le grade de Master' — an establishment diploma of the ENS Louis-Lumière that CONFERS THE GRADE OF MASTER. Under his own rule this counts: a diploma conférant le grade de master is acceptable. But it is the school's own diploma, not a university DNM.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: YES — and it is a low bar on paper. Verbatim: 'Bac +2 minimum (2 ans d'études supérieures dans la même formation)' and age 'Age 27 ans maximum' (for the 2026 session, born after 31 December 1998). The registration page adds the alternative routes: two validated years of higher education in the same state-recognised programme, OR an RNCP level 5 professional certification. A three-year BSc exceeds Bac+2. BUT the school's own guidance on admitted profiles is the real signal, verbatim: 'En Master Son, les candidats admis ont majoritairement un baccalauréat scientifique et sont essentiellement issus d'études à dominante cinéma-audiovisuel (classes préparatoires audiovisuelles, classes préparatoires métiers du son, universités en cinéma, BTS audiovisuel) ou scientifique (classes préparatoires scientifiques, universités en science, écoles d'ingénieurs). Les admis possèdent également une solide culture sonore.' One genuinely encouraging line: 'La pratique d'un instrument n'est pas obligatoire.'
gate: A FULL NATIONAL CONCOURS IN TWO PHASES, AND IT CONTAINS A LISTENING TEST. *** THIS IS THE HEADLINE FINDING OF THE BATCH. *** Phase 2 includes an épreuve named 'Oral d'écoute et d'analyse', described verbatim: 'Le jury propose aux candidats la diffusion d'une courte pièce sonore afin d'apprécier leur capacité d'écoute, d'analyse et d'imagination.' 30 minutes, coefficient 1. This is a critical-listening oral, not a pitch/interval ear-training test and not a performance audition — so it is not automatically fatal for a non-musician — but the batch was filtered as 'no audition' and this is unambiguously an ear-based examination in front of a jury. FULL SON PROGRAMME, verbatim: PHASE 1 (remote, proctored) — 'QCM électricité et électronique' 60 min online, coeff 1; 'QCM mathématiques et physique' 60 min online, coeff 1; 'Création et analyse sonores', coeff 2 (the heaviest weight in phase 1). PHASE 2 (on site, ~1 week in June) — 'Oral d'écoute et d'analyse' 30 min coeff 1; 'Oral de motivation et de culture générale' 30 min coeff 1 (admitted-to-phase-2 candidates must supply a lettre de motivation); 'Oral de sciences et techniques' 15 min prep + 45 min, coeff 1, in three parts including 'une discussion sur des questions de physique' and 'une discussion sur des sujets d'ordre technique en relation avec les domaines d'exploitation du son'. Phases are independent: 'aucune moyenne n'est appliquée entre les différentes phases.' 16 admitted per master, plus a waiting list.
gateType: COMPETITIVE CONCOURS — written technical QCMs + a submitted sound creation + THREE oral juries, one of which ('Oral d'écoute et d'analyse') is an ear/listening examination. Not merely 'portfolio + interview'.
portfolioSpec: PRECISE AND DEMANDING. Verbatim, the 'Création et analyse sonores' épreuve requires the candidate to submit: 'une création sonore d'une durée maximale de 3 min en lien avec une thématique imposée' AND 'une analyse à partir de trois extraits de films disponibles en ligne et d'une question posée.' The theme is set by the school and released on a fixed date (in the 2023 cycle: subjects released Friday 10 March 15h00, submission due Friday 24 March 14h00 — about two weeks' turnaround), uploaded to an online platform. So: ONE original sound piece, maximum 3 minutes, on an imposed theme, plus a written film-sound analysis. Weighted coefficient 2. This is a favourable format in one sense — it is a make-something-from-a-brief test rather than a demand for an existing back-catalogue — but two weeks to produce a jury-grade piece with no prior practice is brutal.
costForTunisian: OUTSIDE THE DIFFÉRENCIÉS REGIME AS RECORDED ON THE SCHOOL'S OWN PAGE — but verify. The programme page states the school charges administrative fees of approximately €104 (CVEC) and about €300 annually in tuition, exempted for scholarship holders. Concours registration fee is separate and real: €120 for the 2026 session (€60 for bursary holders in 2025/26 or 2024/25). CAUTION: décret n° 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 applies to 'les établissements publics d'enseignement supérieur relevant du ministre chargé de l'enseignement supérieur', capping discretionary exemptions at 30% of non-EU students in 2026-27 and 25% in 2027-28, with the master differentiated rate at €3,941/yr. ENS Louis-Lumière's tutelle status determines whether the €3,941 can be applied to him; the school's page still advertises ~€300. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER TO CONFIRM IN WRITING WITH THE SCHOOL BEFORE COUNTING ON IT. As recorded (~€300 + €104 CVEC), the 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' band is right.
funding: French government CROUS bursaries (bourses sur critères sociaux) are referenced by the school as the exemption route, but these are generally not open to a newly-arrived non-EU student without prior French residence. Campus France / French Embassy in Tunis scholarship programmes are the realistic channel and are a SEPARATE, EARLIER application. No programme-specific scholarship found. Amounts and 2027 deadlines UNVERIFIED.
deadline: TWO GATES, AND THEY COLLIDE. (1) The concours itself — PRIOR CYCLE, verbatim: 'du 1 décembre 2025 (15h) jusqu'au mercredi 14 janvier 2026 (15h)'; expect approximately 1 December 2026 – mid-January 2027 for a September 2027 entry. (2) Campus France Tunisie 'Études en France' opens 1 October 2026 and masters close ~15 January 2027. These two run almost exactly in parallel, which is unusually convenient — but he must sit phase-1 written exams in March 2027 and travel to Saint-Denis for phase-2 orals in June 2027 before any visa exists. That travel requirement is a practical obstacle nobody has flagged.
language: French. The school states its formations are in French ('Les formations de l'ENS Louis-Lumière étant en français'), with 'Anglais tout au long du cursus' as a supporting subject. CERTIFICATE DEMANDED, verbatim: candidates without a francophone secondary diploma must present at registration 'la copie d'un test officiel de français équivalent au niveau DELF B2 (ou TCF niveau 4 ou certification équivalente)'. A derogation on timing is possible but admitted candidates must produce it by 30 June. Foreign diplomas need sworn French translation: 'une traduction en langue française par un traducteur assermenté'.
verdictWhy: Sixteen places a year, a national concours against candidates from classes préparatoires métiers du son and audiovisual BTS who have been drilling for this specifically, and the school itself says admitted students already possess 'une solide culture sonore'. He would face two technical QCMs, a jury listening exam, and a three-minute original sound creation on an imposed theme with two weeks to make it — with no music degree, no conservatoire training, no studio experience and no portfolio. The €300 fee is the most attractive number in the whole batch and it is the reason to keep this on a five-year plan, not a 2027 plan.
correction: CONTRADICTS THE RECORDED CHANCE AND THE RECORDED GATE. Recorded chance 'Strong' — it is not; this is one of the hardest competitive entries in French higher education for this field, 16 places nationally. Recorded gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' understates it: the procedure contains an EAR/LISTENING EXAMINATION before a jury ('Oral d'écoute et d'analyse'), which the batch's 'no audition' filter did not catch, plus two technical multiple-choice papers and three separate oral juries. The recorded cost band and language are correct as published, but the cost must be re-confirmed against décret 2026-385.

institution: Le Fresnoy - Studio national des arts contemporains
programme: Cursus / Diplome du Fresnoy (2-year post-graduate artist residency-school)
existsFor2027: YES. Annual call; the most recent published deadline was 'March 11, 2026 — 3pm (Paris time)' for the following intake. Not suspended, not biennial.
awards: NOT a diplôme national de master. It is the 'Diplôme du Fresnoy - Studio national des arts contemporains', an establishment diploma recognised by the Ministry of Culture, which confers the grade de master (level 7). Under his rule this counts — but it is a Ministry-of-Culture artist diploma, not a university DNM.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: NO — HE IS NOT ELIGIBLE. This is the disqualifying fact. Entry requires a diploma PLUS FIVE YEARS of study (i.e. bac+5, level 7), OR a diploma plus seven years of artistic/professional experience with a minimum age of 24. He holds a three-year BSc (bac+3) and has zero post-degree professional or artistic experience. He satisfies neither route. Age is not the problem — the limit is 'aged 35 years maximum on 1st January of the current year, born after 31st December 1990' — the prior-study level is.
gate: Artistic dossier + interview. Preselection is on the portfolio; up to 60 candidates are then interviewed; final selection by a jury including the artistic directors and the school's leadership. No written exam, no ear test, no audition. But this is irrelevant to him until he holds a master's-level qualification.
gateType: Portfolio + interview. No audition, no ear test.
portfolioSpec: SPECIFIED, verbatim: a motivation letter of 3 pages as PDF; project proposals at 1 page per project; visual/audio material as an 'MP4 file, maximum duration 8 minutes' containing video excerpts, photo slideshows or sound samples; and a statement on artists/works of about 20 lines. Submitted online. One MP4, eight minutes maximum — that is the whole creative submission.
costForTunisian: €760/yr, verbatim, for 2026-2027. OUTSIDE the differentiated-fee regime: Le Fresnoy is a Ministry of Culture establishment, not an établissement relevant du ministre chargé de l'enseignement supérieur, so décret n° 2026-385 and the €3,941 master rate do not reach it. The recorded band 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is CORRECT. CVEC applicability to a Ministry-of-Culture school of this type is UNVERIFIED. Note also that Le Fresnoy pays for students' production budgets, which is unusual and materially valuable.
funding: UNVERIFIED — no scholarship scheme was found on the admissions or practical-information pages. The school's production funding for student works is a benefit in kind rather than a scholarship.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE, verbatim: 'March 11, 2026 — 3pm (Paris time)'. Expect approximately March 2027 for the next round. Campus France Tunisie 'Études en France' opens 1 October 2026 and masters close ~15 January 2027 — which falls BEFORE the school's own March deadline, a trap: the binding visa gate closes roughly two months before the school's application does. Exact 2027 dates UNVERIFIED.
language: French for teaching — 'the course is carried out in French' — although applications 'may be submitted in French or English'. No specific French certificate level was stated on the admissions page. UNVERIFIED which certificate is demanded.
verdictWhy: He is flatly ineligible: Le Fresnoy requires bac+5 or seven years of professional artistic practice, and he has a three-year BSc and no experience at all. Nothing else about the programme matters until that changes. It is also not a music-production school — it is a contemporary-art residency for artists who already have a body of work, selected on an eight-minute reel he does not have.
correction: CONTRADICTS THE RECORDED CHANCE. Recorded 'Strong'. The correct value is INELIGIBLE — entry requires bac+5 (level 7) or seven years' professional artistic experience; he has neither. The recorded cost band (Under €1.5k) is confirmed correct at €760/yr, and the recorded gate (portfolio + interview) is correct.
